hypothesis: Wave D18 (C_L3_TIDAL_SETTLING): an orbit settles where it stops flexing (circular, synchronous), by dissipating its flexing F ~ (G M/a^3)^2 n^2 e^2, which grows as P^-6 at fixed masses. The settled state must therefore be reached first at the shortest periods: among binary stars, the fraction of circular orbits falls as the period grows.

observable.quantity: fraction f_k of orbits with e < 0.05 in period bins [1,3), [3,10), [10,30), [30,100), [100,300) d, and the Spearman rank correlation rho of (k, f_k)
observable.domain: spectroscopic binaries of the SB9 catalogue (VizieR B/sb9/orbits), one orbit per system, P between 1 and 300 d

prediction_method.description: SB9 orbits (Seq, Orb, Per, e) downloaded from VizieR after approval; per system the lowest orbit number; e missing or fixed at 0 counts as circular; f_k and rho as in the observable. The script refuses to run unless this card is APPROVED and the data sha256 matches.

fixed_parameters: period bins and the exclusion of P < 1 d (contact systems) are AI choices
one orbit per system: lowest orbit number
PASS needs f_1 >= 0.7 and rho <= -0.9; FAILED if f_1 <= 0.5 or rho >= 0 (AI choices)
any bin with fewer than 30 systems gives INCONCLUSIVE
pass_criterion: PASS if f_1 >= 0.7 and rho <= -0.9: the shortest periods are mostly circular and the circular fraction falls with period.
fail_criterion: FAILED if f_1 <= 0.5 or rho >= 0. INCONCLUSIVE otherwise, or if any bin has fewer than 30 systems.
note: Disclosure: the drafter has not downloaded SB9 for this card, but knows the period-eccentricity relation of binaries in general (short-period orbits are mostly circular, the SB9 paper's abstract mentions it); a PASS is expected and the test is weak. It does not separate tidal settling from circular formation, and authors often fix e = 0 for short periods, which biases f_1 upward (disclosed, not corrected). D18 gives the direction (shorter settles first), not a cutoff period, since it has no timescale. Reading flexing as 'resistance' is an AI interpretation. Nearest theory: Zahn/Hut tidal circularization. Not UET-distinct.
